title: Míriel of the Emerald Veil
type: Scholar · cultural organizer and political speaker
dek: A keeper of knowledge whose research, hospitality and political choices reveal both the reach and the boundaries of Zarathian institutions.

facts.Research: Travel and possible repair; complete success not established
facts.Political record: Speaks after Aria’s death and presents her candidacy

body:
Míriel introduces the Emerald Veil through food, clothing, wealth, celebrations and libraries. Her institution is concerned with the conditions that let a society work. Later scenes connect that civic purpose to arcane research, cultural hospitality and political ambition. She is an expert and an advocate with positions of her own.

January–August 2025 · information and hospitality

At first she describes herself as one of the Emerald Veil, rather than supplying a precise office. In July she welcomes Olokun and his companions, encourages tact and patience and offers introductions. Her expansive description of herself as a keeper of secrets is self-presentation, not proof that she knows every secret.

An August cultural visit exposes a misunderstanding. Olokun has asked for a tour of Zarathian culture; some visitors instead ask about joining factions. Míriel insists on precise information because it determines whom she brings and what she can offer. She explains institutions as ways people support shared work, then encourages the visitors to share what they have learned.

Her hospitality is therefore purposeful. She wants outsiders to understand how a people lives, rather than see only courts, military strength or powerful mages.

Research with boundaries

In July she tells Olokun that work has begun on crossing the Veil and potentially healing it. She says the Gate spell bypasses the Void. When he asks about the Gate through which the adventurers arrived, she explicitly says she knows nothing of that specific event and would like to research it.

Her distinction matters: an expert’s account of a spell does not settle the history of every Gate. Possible healing is a research aim, not a completed restoration. Míriel also emphasizes caution about experiments whose effects are not understood.

In October she says the Emerald Veil’s mightiest magi can open great Gates when a destination is known, while admitting that the group lacks knowledge of where to go. Powerful transport and comprehensive geography are different capabilities. Her admission that her people rarely venture beyond their own shores preserves the limits of their expertise.

Magic as coordinated work

Her research is supported by other practitioners and by planning. During the November preparations she reports uncertainty over the destination before ordering archmages to open Gates and send legions through. The scene shows institutional capacity alongside incomplete information; it does not establish that every member of the Emerald Veil can perform the same work.

After Aria · grief and ambition

After Aria’s death, Míriel’s response is far less neutral than the image of a detached scholar might suggest. She describes a broken-hearted people and argues that the outsiders should be exiled, except for Magnus. This is her proposed response, not proof that the punishment was enacted or that every outsider bears equal responsibility.

In December she presents her own candidacy while also praising Magnus as a returned hero around whom the people might unite. She says she prefers arcane work and the subtlety of words to martial display. The public speech establishes political participation, but leaves her full motive unresolved. Her support for Magnus does not resolve accusations against him or replace Bowene’s later history.

The open history

Her formal rank, complete research outcomes, authority within the Emerald Veil and later political position remain unresolved. She is not merged with the separately named Captain Miriel. Her expertise, institutional loyalties and political judgments should remain visible together rather than turning her into an omniscient or politically neutral voice.
